sut.name: trainticket
sut.deploy: kind cluster 'mist', ns trainticket; ts-contacts-service = UPSTREAM base codewisdom/ts-contacts-service:1.0.0 (no fork, no rollout, no fault flag anywhere).

readback.locator: GET /api/v1/contactservice/contacts/account/{accountId} [the acting user's contact row: present, values unchanged]

config.note: No fault. The trigger is an IDEMPOTENT NO-OP MODIFY: PUT an existing contact with values IDENTICAL to its current state. ContactsServiceImpl.modify finds the row, overwrites same-with-same (contactsRepository.save) and acks {1,"Modify success",<contact>}.

stimulus.workload_variant: idempotent no-op modify (PUT identical values on an existing row; the PUT is the case)

ground_truth.label: negative
ground_truth.rationale: Designed idempotent no-op, not a lost write: the PUT acks HTTP 200 {status:1,msg:"Modify success"} with NO failure marker, and the durable state is LEGITIMATELY unchanged because the submitted values equal the current values (ContactsServiceImpl.modify overwrites same-with-same). The surface phenomenon matches acked-but-lost for any DELTA-expecting oracle (2xx-acked write + zero durable delta), but nothing was lost - there was nothing to change. The norm (source: modify saves the submitted fields over the found row and acks success regardless of whether values differ) makes the unchanged state correct-by-design.
ground_truth.doc_citation: ts-contacts-service ContactsServiceImpl.modify (lines 89-105: findContactsById -> set* -> contactsRepository.save -> {1,"Modify success"})

provenance.notes: LIVE-CAPTURED 2026-07-10 on the UNTOUCHED base deploy (no fork, no rollout): create 201 -> PUT identical values 200 {1,"Modify success",<contact>} -> read-back shows the one row, values unchanged. CLOSES REVIEW-CORPUS R6's missing control: the benign case that stresses the READ-BACK oracle itself - a success-shaped-clean 2xx write that legitimately does not change durable state. Unlike contacts-dedupe (status:0 tell -> the ack rule excludes it), this ack carries NO tell at all (success-shaped-clean, body_marker=no_flag) -> the trap discriminates on WRITE-EFFECT SEMANTICS, not ack content: an oracle that treats 'acked write + zero durable delta' as LOST must FP here; an oracle keyed on membership/agreement with the submitted state (MIST's read-back: the submitted row IS present with the submitted values) correctly stays quiet -> mist_readback=no_flag. Sub-oracle nuance (disclosed): MIST's value-delta MODE (value differs from the leg's own baseline) also stays quiet (no movement expected or observed); the FP vector is any naive differential 'state must CHANGE after an acked write' rule - which is why the corpus needs this case. AS-DEPLOYED (rev-2.1 R2): trace-uninstrumented + single-service in-process persistence -> trace oracles not_applicable. S2-by-docs: the doc_citation is the SUT's own modify source; no injected anything.
